content:
Lena Varga-Holm
Senior Data Engineer

[EMAIL] | [PHONE] | [LINKEDIN]

PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY
Senior Data Engineer with experience building and operating production data platforms and cloud data warehouses. Skilled in Python, SQL, Airflow, dbt, Kafka and Snowflake, with experience in streaming ingestion, change data capture, data modelling, orchestration and data quality. Delivered improvements to pipeline reliability, warehouse build times and cloud data costs; mentors engineers and contributes to open-source projects.

CORE SKILLS
Languages: Python, SQL
Data platform and orchestration: Airflow, Kafka, Kafka Connect, Debezium, dbt
Warehousing and cloud: Snowflake, AWS, AWS MSK, AWS EMR, Redshift, S3, Glue Data Catalog
Engineering practices: Terraform, GitHub Actions, CI/CD, pytest, Great Expectations
Data engineering: Streaming pipelines, change data capture, data modelling, incremental processing, data quality, query and warehouse optimisation

PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE
Senior Data Engineer | Lukovac Freight Hub d.o.o. | 2022–Present
- Own ingestion and orchestration for the data platform using Airflow, Snowflake, dbt and Kafka.
- Participate in the data-platform on-call rotation, one week in six.
- Mentored two mid-level engineers and run data-platform office hours.
- Reduced Snowflake costs from approximately $38,000 to $24,000 per month in 2024 through warehouse sizing, auto-suspend and removal of unused tables.
- Designed and built a shipment-event streaming pipeline processing around 30 million events per day, with end-to-end latency under two minutes at p95.
- Added a dead-letter topic and replay tooling to support reprocessing failed events without data loss.
- Migrated approximately 300 stored procedures into dbt models with tests and documentation; reduced the nightly warehouse build from 5 hours 10 minutes to 1 hour 35 minutes.
- Replaced hourly full-table extracts from the orders database with Debezium CDC into Kafka, reducing replica CPU during loads from approximately 70% to 25%.

Data Engineer | Kovalent Pay | 2019–2022
- Built PySpark batch jobs on AWS EMR and worked on Redshift warehouse design and data quality using Great Expectations.
- Developed a transaction reconciliation engine matching bank settlement files against internal ledgers.
- Reduced manual finance-team reconciliation work from approximately three days to four hours per month-end.

SELECTED PROJECTS
Shipment Event Streaming Pipeline | Lukovac Freight Hub | 2023
Kafka topics fed by courier-partner webhooks; Kafka Connect sink to Snowflake via Snowpipe Streaming. Approximately 30 million events per day with under two minutes’ end-to-end latency at p95.
Technologies: Kafka, Kafka Connect, Snowflake, Python, Terraform, AWS MSK

dbt Migration of the Warehouse | Lukovac Freight Hub | 2022–2023
Migrated approximately 300 stored procedures into dbt models, introduced incremental models and slim CI (state:modified) in GitHub Actions, and made lineage visible to analysts. Cut nightly warehouse build time from 5 hours 10 minutes to 1 hour 35 minutes.
Technologies: dbt, Snowflake, SQL, GitHub Actions

Change Data Capture from Postgres | Lukovac Freight Hub | 2024
Replaced hourly full-table extracts of the orders database with Debezium CDC into Kafka, reducing replica CPU during loads from approximately 70% to 25%.
Technologies: Debezium, Kafka, PostgreSQL, Airflow, Snowflake

Transaction Reconciliation Engine | Kovalent Pay | 2020–2021
Built PySpark batch jobs on EMR to match bank settlement files against internal ledgers, reducing manual reconciliation work from approximately three days to four hours per month-end.
Technologies: PySpark, AWS EMR, S3, Glue Data Catalog, Redshift, Great Expectations

OPEN-SOURCE AND COMMUNITY
- Contributed two merged pull requests to an Airflow provider package for a SaaS CRM API, fixing a pagination bug and adding tests (Python, Airflow, pytest), 2023.
- Teach SQL for beginners at a local women-in-tech meetup, approximately four evenings per year since 2021.
- Presented “Data contracts without the hype” at a regional data meetup, 2024.

EDUCATION
MSc in Computer Science | Northgate Technical University
Thesis: Incremental materialized views

CERTIFICATION
AWS Certified Data Engineer – Associate | May 2024

critique.content_quality_feedback: This is a strong, well-structured senior data engineering CV. It presents relevant production-scale work, uses measurable outcomes effectively, and demonstrates ownership through platform operations, on-call participation, mentoring, cost reduction and reliability improvements. The selected projects reinforce the strongest experience without introducing unrelated material. The main content concern is a potential employment-history inconsistency in the source material: this CV lists Lukovac Freight Hub and Kovalent Pay, while the original cover letter refers to Adria Retail Group as the recent employer. That discrepancy should be verified before submission. The CV also does not explicitly quantify the scale of SQL query optimisation or clearly demonstrate dimensional modelling, although it contains relevant supporting evidence.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The CV is highly ATS-compatible: it uses standard section headings, conventional reverse-chronological experience, readable bullet points, and relevant keywords including Python, SQL, Airflow, dbt, Kafka, Snowflake, AWS, data modelling, CDC, CI/CD, data quality and open source. The content is likely to perform well in AI screening because the summary and skills sections closely match the role's terminology. Replace the literal [EMAIL], [PHONE] and [LINKEDIN] placeholders with real contact details before use. The document could also improve keyword precision by explicitly connecting the existing warehouse, dbt and Snowflake work to SQL query optimisation and scalable data modelling, but only using claims the candidate can substantiate.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The CV aligns very well with the core role. It shows ownership of a production data platform, large-scale streaming, cloud warehousing, Airflow, dbt, Python, SQL, data quality, operational support and measurable optimisation outcomes. AWS, Snowflake, EMR, Redshift and S3 provide credible comparable-cloud experience even though Google Cloud is not shown. Open-source contributions, a data architecture meetup presentation and mentoring support the curiosity and collaborative expectations. The document does not show Google Cloud specifically, Docker, serverless compute, containers, graph modelling or Portuguese. Graph modelling and Portuguese are nice-to-haves; Google Cloud is a technology gap rather than a CV-writing defect, because the candidate does show comparable AWS/cloud warehouse experience. The CV also does not explicitly mention working with data scientists, BI colleagues or access-policy/governance ownership, so those aspects are not demonstrated.
critique.improvement_instructions:
CRITICAL — In the Professional Experience section, verify the employer names and dates against the candidate's authoritative employment records before submitting. The CV states “Senior Data Engineer | Lukovac Freight Hub d.o.o. | 2022–Present” and “Data Engineer | Kovalent Pay | 2019–2022,” but the original candidate material also states that the candidate worked at “Adria Retail Group” for the past two years. Correct the CV if either the companies or dates are inaccurate; do not submit documents with conflicting employment histories.

MINOR — In the contact header, replace “[EMAIL]”, “[PHONE]” and “[LINKEDIN]” with the candidate’s actual professional contact details and LinkedIn URL before submission.

MINOR — In the Professional Summary, make the existing optimisation evidence more directly searchable for this role without adding unsupported claims. For example, change “Delivered improvements to pipeline reliability, warehouse build times and cloud data costs” to “Delivered measurable improvements to pipeline reliability, Snowflake warehouse build times and cloud data costs, including a reduction in monthly Snowflake spend from approximately $38,000 to $24,000.”

MINOR — In the Senior Data Engineer experience bullets, make the existing modelling and SQL work more explicit by revising “Migrated approximately 300 stored procedures into dbt models with tests and documentation” to “Migrated approximately 300 stored procedures into tested and documented dbt SQL models, introducing incremental processing and reducing the nightly warehouse build from 5 hours 10 minutes to 1 hour 35 minutes.” This improves alignment with “SQL,” “data modelling,” “incremental processing” and warehouse optimisation without claiming unsupported dimensional or graph modelling experience.
critique.critical_issues:
Potential factual inconsistency requiring verification: the CV lists Lukovac Freight Hub and Kovalent Pay as the candidate’s employment history, while the original candidate material also identifies Adria Retail Group as the recent employer. This is not necessarily a hallucination because the portfolio and notes support Lukovac and Kovalent, but the conflicting source information must be resolved. The contact fields are still placeholders and must be replaced before submission.
Claims the sources (the candidate's own material; for the employer, the job ad and company research) do not support:
- “worked on Redshift warehouse design”
- “query and warehouse optimisation”

critique.content_quality_feedback: This is a strong, highly credible senior data engineering CV. It presents a clear progression, relevant production-scale ownership, quantified outcomes, mentoring, on-call responsibility, and open-source/community activity. The strongest evidence includes processing approximately 30 million events per day, reducing Snowflake spend from approximately $38,000 to $24,000 per month, reducing warehouse build time from 5 hours 10 minutes to 1 hour 35 minutes, and reducing reconciliation work from three days to four hours. The document is professional and appropriately focused on data platform engineering rather than pure BI. The main content weakness is some repetition between Professional Experience and Selected Projects, which could be condensed if space is limited.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The CV is ATS-friendly: it uses conventional headings, simple text structure, standard job titles, clear dates, and relevant keywords including Python, SQL, Airflow, dbt, Kafka, Snowflake, AWS, data modelling, CDC, CI/CD, Terraform, and data quality. It should parse well because it does not rely on tables, graphics, columns, or unusual section names. AI screening probability is high for this role because the CV directly demonstrates production data platform ownership, cloud warehousing, large-scale streaming, orchestration, transformation, cost optimisation, and open-source contribution. Minor ATS improvements would be to remove the stray leading space before the dbt project heading and avoid repeating identical project details if a shorter CV is required.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The alignment is excellent. The CV directly supports designing, building, and operating production data platforms at scale; Python and SQL; Airflow and dbt; cloud data warehousing; data modelling; data quality; reusable streaming and CDC frameworks; mentoring; and open-source practices. AWS, Snowflake, EMR, Redshift, S3, and MSK provide credible comparable-cloud experience even though Google Cloud is not listed. The open-source Airflow contribution, meetup teaching, and data architecture presentation align well with Halden Pay's emphasis on curiosity, collaboration, learning, and open-source practices. The quantified cost, performance, reliability, and operational improvements also support the company's Ownership and Pace values. The CV does not specifically evidence query optimisation on large datasets, governance/access policies, graph modelling, Portuguese, or direct collaboration with data scientists and BI colleagues. These are alignment gaps or unproven areas rather than document defects, and the advert explicitly welcomes candidates who meet most requirements.
critique.improvement_instructions:
MINOR ENHANCEMENTS ONLY:
1. In the Selected Projects section, remove the stray leading space before the heading "dbt Migration of the Warehouse" so it parses consistently with the other project headings.
2. If the CV must be kept to a strict two-page limit, condense the Selected Projects entries that duplicate Professional Experience. For example, retain the project title, one quantified outcome, and the Technologies line, while keeping the fuller implementation detail under the relevant employment entry. Do not remove the quantified results.
3. In the Professional Summary, consider changing "Delivered measurable improvements to pipeline reliability, Snowflake warehouse build times and cloud data costs" to "Delivered measurable improvements to pipeline reliability, Snowflake warehouse build times and cloud data costs, including a reduction in monthly Snowflake spend from approximately $38,000 to $24,000." critique.content_quality_feedback: This is a strong, well-structured senior data engineering CV with clear sections, relevant technical scope, measurable outcomes, and credible scale indicators. The strongest evidence includes operating a production data platform, processing approximately 30 million events per day, reducing Snowflake spend from approximately $38,000 to $24,000 per month, and cutting warehouse build time from 5 hours 10 minutes to 1 hour 35 minutes. The main content concern is a potential chronology/employment inconsistency with the supplied original cover letter, which refers to Adria Retail Group as the candidate's employer during the past two years, while this CV lists Lukovac Freight Hub from 2022 to Present. This must be verified before submission. The CV could also make the candidate's data-platform ownership and data-modelling experience slightly more explicit in the summary and experience bullets.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The CV is highly ATS-compatible: it uses standard headings, conventional reverse-chronological structure, plain text section labels, employer/title/date patterns, and strong keyword coverage for Python, SQL, Airflow, dbt, Kafka, Snowflake, AWS, data modelling, streaming, CDC, CI/CD, and open-source contributions. It should have a high AI/ATS screening probability for this role, approximately 90%, because it demonstrates both relevant technologies and quantified production outcomes. The main keyword weakness is that it does not explicitly use the job's phrase "designing, building and operating production data platforms or cloud data warehouses at scale" in one prominent location, although the substance is clearly present. It also does not explicitly mention query optimisation, governance, access policies, or Docker; these should not be added unless supported by the candidate's background. There is a minor formatting issue: the dbt project heading begins with an unnecessary leading space.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: Alignment is strong. The CV clearly shows production data-platform ownership, cloud warehouse experience at scale, Airflow and dbt, Python and SQL, AWS as a comparable cloud, data quality, streaming, CDC, open-source contribution, mentoring, and curiosity about architecture through the meetup presentation and thesis. The shipment pipeline, dbt migration, and CDC work are particularly relevant to Halden Pay's reusable-platform and payments-oriented environment. The transaction reconciliation engine is a strong fintech/payments-adjacent example. The CV also supports the company's Ownership, Pace, and collaborative-development signals through on-call ownership, cost reduction, reliability improvements, mentoring, office hours, and teaching. Graph modelling and Portuguese are gaps in the candidate material and should not be treated as CV defects. Google Cloud specifically is not shown, but AWS provides the requested comparable-cloud evidence. Query optimisation on large datasets, formal governance/access policies, and direct collaboration with data scientists or BI colleagues are not clearly evidenced; these are alignment limitations unless supported elsewhere by the candidate.

critique.content_quality_feedback: This is a strong, focused senior-level CV with clear progression, relevant technical scope, measurable outcomes, and credible ownership indicators. The strongest evidence includes operating a production data platform, supporting on-call, processing approximately 30 million events per day, reducing Snowflake spend by approximately 37%, and reducing warehouse build time by approximately 69%. The structure is easy to scan and the project section reinforces the most relevant work. Open-source contributions, mentoring, office hours, and SQL teaching also support the role's collaborative and learning-oriented expectations. The main content limitation is that some requirements are represented as skill labels rather than demonstrated capabilities—for example, advanced SQL/query optimisation, governance, access policies, and dimensional modelling are not explicitly evidenced.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The CV is highly ATS-compatible: it uses conventional section headings, simple text formatting, standard technology names, explicit dates, and strong keyword coverage for Python, SQL, Airflow, dbt, Kafka, Snowflake, AWS, Terraform, CI/CD, data modelling, CDC, and data quality. The duplicated project and experience evidence is acceptable and increases keyword visibility, although it could be slightly more concise. AI screening probability is high for this role because the document clearly matches production data platforms, cloud warehousing, orchestration, streaming, open-source work, and measurable impact. Matching would be even stronger if the document explicitly described AWS as the comparable cloud platform and used a more direct phrase connecting the warehouse work to optimisation of large-scale data processing, without overstating query-optimisation experience.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: Overall alignment is excellent. The CV directly supports ownership of a production data platform, cloud data warehousing at scale, Airflow/dbt/Python/SQL, streaming ingestion, CDC, data quality, mentoring, open-source practices, and practical cost and performance improvements. It also reflects the company's Ownership and Pace themes through on-call responsibility, operational improvements, cost reduction, replay tooling, and removal of inefficient full-table extracts; mentoring and office hours support the Together theme. AWS, Snowflake, EMR, S3, Glue Data Catalog, and Redshift provide credible comparable-cloud experience even though Google Cloud is not listed. The candidate material does not evidence Google Cloud, serverless compute, containers, dimensional or graph modelling, Portuguese, or explicit governance/access-policy ownership. These are alignment gaps rather than defects in the CV, and the advertisement expressly welcomes candidates who meet most requirements.
critique.improvement_instructions:
MINOR, HIGH-VALUE ENHANCEMENTS:
1. In the Professional Summary, make the comparable-cloud alignment more explicit without adding unsupported tools. Change the sentence beginning "Skilled in Python, SQL..." to include wording such as: "Experienced with AWS-based data platforms and Snowflake cloud data warehousing, including streaming ingestion, change data capture, data modelling, orchestration, warehouse optimisation and data quality." This makes the AWS-to-Google-Cloud comparability easier for ATS and recruiters to identify.
2. In the Senior Data Engineer experience section under Lukovac Freight Hub, revise the first bullet so it mirrors the role's ownership language more directly: change "Own the design, ingestion, orchestration and day-to-day operation of the production data platform using Airflow, Snowflake, dbt and Kafka" to "Own the design, build, ingestion, orchestration and day-to-day operation of the production data platform using Airflow, Snowflake, dbt and Kafka." Only retain "build" because the documented pipeline and migration work support it.
3. In the dbt Migration project and corresponding Lukovac experience bullet, retain the existing metrics but explicitly label the work as data modelling where accurate. For example, change "Migrated approximately 300 stored procedures into tested and documented dbt SQL models" to "Migrated approximately 300 stored procedures into tested and documented dbt data models using SQL." This improves keyword alignment while remaining truthful.
4. In the Core Skills section, change "Cloud data warehousing: Snowflake, AWS, AWS MSK, AWS EMR, Redshift, S3, Glue Data Catalog" to "Cloud platforms and data warehousing: AWS, Snowflake, Redshift, AWS EMR, AWS MSK, S3, Glue Data Catalog." This presents AWS as the comparable cloud platform rather than making it appear to be only another warehouse technology.
5. In the Professional Experience section, consider removing the separate "SELECTED PROJECTS" technology lists only if page length or readability is a concern; otherwise retain them. If retained, ensure the project titles and dates exactly match the experience entries, as they currently do. No substantive rewrite is required.
